questions.text: In which country can you find this famous statue?
questions.funFact: Christ the Redeemer stands 30 meters tall and was completed in 1931.

questions.text: This flaming crater is known as the 'Door to Hell'. Where is it?
questions.funFact: The Darvaza gas crater has been burning continuously since 1971.

questions.text: Which country is home to this ancient temple?
questions.funFact: Borobudur is the world's largest Buddhist temple, built in the 9th century.

questions.text: This iconic mountain is a symbol of which country?
questions.funFact: Mount Fuji is 3,776 meters high and last erupted in 1707.

questions.text: This colorful town with blue and white houses is in which country?
questions.funFact: Sidi Bou Said's blue and white color scheme was established by a French baron in 1915.

questions.text: This burrito is a traditional dish from which country?
questions.funFact: The burrito is believed to have originated in Northern Mexico in the 19th century.

questions.text: This glass noodle stir-fry dish called Japchae is from which country?
questions.funFact: Japchae was originally created for a royal banquet in the 17th century.

questions.text: Fish and chips is a beloved national dish of which country?
questions.funFact: The first fish and chip shop in the UK opened in the 1860s.

questions.text: This tagine dish with chicken and olives is from which country?
questions.funFact: The tagine is both the name of the dish and the conical clay pot it's cooked in.

questions.text: This communal hot pot is a traditional way of eating in which country?
questions.funFact: Hot pot has been a Chinese tradition for over 1,000 years, especially popular in Sichuan.

questions.text: The ancient city of Petra, carved into rose-red cliffs, is in which country?
questions.funFact: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom and was lost to the Western world for centuries.

questions.text: The Aztec Empire was centered in what is now which country?
questions.funFact: The Aztec capital Tenochtitlan was built on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325.

questions.text: The ancient kingdom of Aksum was located in which modern-day country?
questions.funFact: The Kingdom of Aksum was one of the four great powers of the ancient world.

questions.text: The Silk Road connected China with which other major civilization?
questions.funFact: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes spanning over 6,400 km.

questions.text: The Great Zimbabwe ruins are found in which African country?
questions.funFact: Great Zimbabwe was the capital of a thriving trading empire from the 11th to 15th century.

questions.text: Where is the Sahara Desert located?
questions.funFact: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world, almost as large as the United States.

questions.text: Can you locate the Amazon River on the map?
questions.funFact: The Amazon River carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

questions.text: Where is the Himalaya mountain range?
questions.funFact: The Himalayas contain 9 of the 10 highest peaks in the world, including Mount Everest.

questions.text: Where is the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.funFact: The Great Barrier Reef is the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space.

questions.text: Can you locate Lake Baikal on the map?
questions.funFact: Lake Baikal is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake in the world.

questions.text: The Day of the Dead (Dia de los Muertos) is celebrated in which country?
questions.funFact: Day of the Dead is a celebration of life and death, with roots in Aztec tradition.

questions.text: Diwali, the Festival of Lights, originated in which country?
questions.funFact: Diwali is celebrated by over 1 billion people worldwide across multiple religions.

questions.text: The Haka is a traditional war dance of which indigenous people?
questions.funFact: The All Blacks rugby team famously performs the Haka before every match.

questions.text: Carnival with elaborate samba parades is most famous in which city?
questions.funFact: Rio Carnival attracts over 2 million people per day during celebrations.

questions.text: The Lantern Festival marks the end of Chinese New Year in which country?
questions.funFact: The Lantern Festival dates back over 2,000 years to the Han Dynasty.

questions.text: The kimono is the traditional garment of which country?
questions.funFact: The word kimono literally means 'thing to wear' in Japanese.

questions.text: The colorful kente cloth is traditionally woven by which people?
questions.funFact: Kente cloth patterns have specific meanings and were once reserved for royalty.

questions.text: The sari is a traditional draped garment from which country?
questions.funFact: The sari has been worn for over 5,000 years, making it one of the oldest garments.

questions.text: The hanbok is the traditional clothing of which country?
questions.funFact: Hanbok is characterized by vibrant colors and simple lines without pockets.

questions.text: The poncho is a traditional garment originating from which region?
questions.funFact: The poncho has been worn by indigenous peoples of the Andes for over 500 years.

questions.text: ⭐ BONUS — Where is Ericsson's Headquarters? Drop a pin!
questions.funFact: Ericsson was founded in 1876 and is headquartered in Kista, Stockholm.
